newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares rise on hopes of Chidambaram's return.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares rise on hopes of Chidambaram's return.

text.p: Delhi share prices rose in afternoon trade on Monday on hopes that former finance minister P. Chidambaram might return to the United Front coalition government, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index was up 9.01 points at 806.68 at 12:45 p.m. (0715 GMT).
"The decision of the Tamil Maanila Congress to join the government would decide the fate of the market," said Yogesh Sethi of brokers Vinayaka Investments.

Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) on Sunday authorised its leader, G.K. Moopanar, to decide whether the regional party should join India's new government. A decision is expected to be announced by Wednesday.

The TMC, part of the centre-left United Front coalition, decided on April 19 to stay out of the government after the alliance chose Inder Kumar Gujral instead of Moopanar as its leader and new prime minister.
Gujral has not appointed a finance minister in his cabinet, signalling the slot was open for Chidambaram. Chidambaram's tax-cutting 1997/98 (April-March) budget has yet to win parliamentary approval.
State Bank of India rose 1.40 rupees to 319.10 on buying by foreign investors, brokers said.
TISCO edged up 2.05 rupees to 183.25 on foreign buying, brokers said.
